roadmap.scope: SLICE 1 ONLY: claim_domain::identity_link core, identity link/verify/list/forget, v7 checks + read/write/purge ports, GithubPort::read_person_by_id + DD-GDL-11 contract test, reserved-predicate guard (claim counter exempt, D-b), GDL-D13 check-arch rules.

conventions.paradigm: ADR-007: decisions pure in claim-domain; adapters and cli verbs do I/O only.
conventions.test_paradigm: Acceptance: example-based subprocess. Pure core: proptest against the CORE oracles. Adapters: real DuckDB / real HTTP adapter against FakeGithubAccounts, never mocked.
conventions.scenario_fns: `<cargo test target>::<fn>` (identity_link = tests/acceptance/identity_link.rs, identity_link_core = tests/acceptance/identity_link_core.rs), in activation order.
conventions.test_edit_allow_list: Test-file edits limited to: removing the #[ignore] of a named scenario_fn; replacing the named sut_* body with ONE real call plus view mapping (DD-GDL-16). Forbidden: assertions, oracles, strategies, universe slots, helpers, test names. The GREEN diff must match.
conventions.test_runs: Scoped targets only, never the workspace. libtest runs tests matching ANY positional filter (library/test/src/cli.rs), so `-- f1 f2` is used.
conventions.check_arch: `cargo xtask check-arch` (.cargo/config.toml alias) + `cargo test -p xtask`; each new rule ships a synthetic-violation test.
conventions.link_predicate_api: Q-RM-5: claim_domain::identity_link exposes the link predicate through its API (e.g. link_predicate()); readers select candidate rows with it; project() decides.

phases.name: Slice-01 — Prove, sign, publish, re-check and locally forget a GitHub↔DID link from the CLI

steps.name: Walking skeleton: `identity link github jeffbailey --yes` publishes the proven sameAs link and `identity list` shows it verified today
steps.description: Thinnest WS-GDL-1 thread. claim-domain gains check_link (same-id case), ProvenLink → LinkDraft → UnsignedClaim and record JSON (encoder move, Q-RM-1), thin project and link_view. NEW `identity link` signs and publishes via the single publish path, bypassing the compose step (Q-RM-4).
criteria: WS-GDL-1: linking exits 0, prints the record ID and `openlore claim retract <id>`; the published record is did:plc:test-jeff sameAs github:jeffbailey with profile and account-number evidence.
WS-GDL-1: `identity list` shows github:jeffbailey verified today; the store gains exactly one claim, its file, one published record, one verified check.
CORE-4: an encoded link decodes, hashes to the same CID twice, and projects back to the same DID, login and account number.
Before the move, a new golden test pins today's claim_record_json bytes for a publish and a retract record; it passes unchanged after the move.
check-arch fails when the `sameAs` literal or link-predicate constant appears outside claim-domain::identity_link.
green: cargo test -p cli --test identity_link_readers -- reading_a_person_whose_bio_names_a_did a_possible_rename_among_inferred_people
steps.implementation_notes: Remove WS-GDL-1's #[ignore] in the commit it goes green. No existing test pins the record bytes (review_app_core.rs only calls claim_record_json), so the golden comes first: it calls review_domain::plans::claim_record_json, is committed green on today's encoder, and must pass unchanged through the re-export after the move. Q-RM-1: claim_record_json, reference_type, CLAIM_COLLECTION move together; review-domain re-exports; nothing copied. Q-RM-4: verbs/identity_link.rs builds the claim via LinkDraft and gets the predicate via the API. Confirm writes one check + the signed claim (ADR-085 §7). CORE-2 waits for 01-07 (DD-GDL-16).
steps.mutation_note: Kill: codec evidence-order or confidence changes (CORE-4, WS); removing the compose-only rule (its synthetic-violation test).

steps.name: A link is refused unless a fresh bio read names my exact DID; the preview writes nothing; bad logins and unreadable GitHub change nothing
steps.description: Complete `identity link` refusal and preview paths: plan-returning preview (ADR-085 §7), bio verdict refusals, login validated before any request (ADR-076), GitHub failures fail closed (ADR-085 §4, DD-GDL-13).
criteria: IL-2: without confirmation Jeff sees the exact record, that it is public, and that retraction withdraws without erasing; nothing published or recorded.
IL-3: six bio rows and a missing account refuse with exit 1, verdict token and plain phrase; nothing published or recorded.
IL-4: Jeff's DID proves the account in each of the four bio positions.
IL-6: rate limit, outage or rejected token: told GitHub could not be read; nothing published or recorded; token never printed.
IL-7: each malformed login exits 1 with `not a GitHub username`; GitHub is never asked.
green: cargo test -p cli --test identity_link -- jeff_sees_exactly no_link_is_made jeffs_did_proves when_github_cannot_be_read a_malformed_github_username
cargo test -p cli --test identity_link_readers -- reading_a_person_whose_bio_names_a_did a_possible_rename_among_inferred_people
steps.implementation_notes: Only a confirmed, passing link writes a check (ADR-085 §7). Confirmation per Q-GDL-D2.

steps.name: An Active link is not linked twice, a retracted one can be, a second account links alongside, and a link survives an unreachable repo host
steps.description: link_view folds same-author lineage (ADR-085 §5, reusing claim-domain retraction rules). `identity link` honours D-a, D-g, A-4; on a repo-host failure it keeps the signed link and its check (Q-GDL-D1 wording).
criteria: IL-5: re-linking an Active link exits 1 `already linked`, naming `openlore identity verify`; nothing signed, published or recorded.
IL-14: after `claim retract`, linking again publishes a new record ID, shown verified.
IL-10: a second account links; `identity list` shows both verified for Jeff.
IL-9a: repo host unreachable: Jeff is told so and to retry with `openlore claim publish`; the link shows verified; nothing published.
IL-9b: once the host is back, `claim publish <id>` puts the link on the PDS under that record ID.

steps.name: `identity verify` re-checks each Active link with one request, keeps earlier checks, shows a lost proof as `proof gone`, and records nothing when GitHub fails
steps.description: NEW `identity verify` holding check read/write and GithubPort only (ADR-085 §7). Appends one check per decided re-check; never retracts (GDL-D5, C-GDL-6). Empty store and GitHub failures change nothing (ADR-085 §4).
criteria: IV-8: with no links Jeff is told there are none to verify; GitHub is never asked.
IV-1: once the bio drops the DID, verify reports did_missing; the list shows `proof gone`; the published link is untouched; one did_missing check is added.
IV-2: with the DID back, one request restores verified-today; earlier checks are kept.
IV-9: both accounts re-checked, one request each, both verified.
IV-6: rate limit, outage or rejected token: nothing recorded, token never printed, link still verified.

steps.name: Renames and re-registrations are told apart by account number; unfollowable GitHub answers change nothing; recorded fixtures pin the profile shape
steps.description: EXTEND GithubPort with read_person_by_id (UC-9); at most one same-host redirect (N-2). check_link completes ADR-085 §4. DD-GDL-11 recorded-fixture contract test.
criteria: IV-3a: after a rename with the old login gone, GitHub is asked for the old login then the account number; the link shows verified as github:jeff-b.
IV-3b: the next re-check asks GitHub once, for jeff-b. IV-4: a forwarded old login: at most two requests, no account-number request, verified as jeff-b.
IV-5: a re-registered login resolves to the renamed account, verified; a deleted account is account_not_found, proof gone.
IV-10: chained or cross-host forwarding records nothing; the link stays verified.
